content:
sophie-support: Hey team — customer (org: acme-markets, tenant: t-08b3) reports their monthly credits dropped to 0 mid-run during a 12-minute streaming generation. They expected refill at 00:00 UTC but started getting 429s ~23:57 UTC. stream_id=st-77a, user reports UI showed >1000 tokens remaining right before the last chunk.

michael-support: Oof. Do we have the 429 payload and the dashboard snapshot? Also, what timezone is the tenant configured in?

sophie-support: Pasted 429 body from customer: `{"error":"quota_exceeded","retry_after":60}`. Customer screenshot shows tenant tz set to America/Los_Angeles. They claim dashboard still displayed 1,200 tokens at 23:56 local.

elaine-engineer: Two quick hypotheses: 1) UI cache/display lag vs backend refill timing (dashboard uses cached aggregate), 2) long-running streaming requests may double-count tokens if chunk boundary accounting overlaps with refill window.

ops-bot: Incident created #INC-2023-7145 — tagging billing and infra. Auto-attach logs from stream_id=st-77a.

michael-support: Sophie, can you ask for a HAR or raw websocket dump? Need exact sequence of frames near the 429. If they can’t share, ask for a sanitized timeline (frame timestamps + token delta).

sophie-support: Asked for websocket dump. Customer provided minimal timeline: start 23:52:10 UTC, steady token burn, last successful frame 23:56:40, then 429 at 23:57:02, then UI showed refill at 00:00:05 local (PST) but API still 429 until 00:00:54.

elaine-engineer: That pattern matches an edge where the refill job runs at 00:00:00 UTC but streaming inflight accounting finalization occurs after the refill window due to last-frame reconciliation. Possible scenario: backend finalizes in-flight usage after the refill mark, so UI (which reads the new bucket) shows refill, but finalized usage from in-flight frames then exhausts the freshly refilled bucket.

jordan-billing: If that's true, customer experienced a race: finalization consumption applied after window boundary. We can offer a one-time prorated credit and follow up with engineering for a long-term fix (either hold refill until all inflight finalize or make refill atomic with finalization).

michael-support: For immediate triage we should: 1) issue a temporary credit to unblock the customer, 2) capture repro: reproduce with long streaming session crossing refill boundary, 3) instrument finalization & refill ordering logs. Elaine, can you add a trace flag to the refill job for this tenant tomorrow midnight and force a repro in staging?

elaine-engineer: Will do. Steps I’ll run in staging: 1) spawn streaming client that sends partial frames over ~8–15 minutes, 2) set tenant timezone to America/Los_Angeles, 3) advance staging clock to cross refill at midnight, 4) capture finalization event timestamps and bucket deltas. I’ll post logs here.

jordan-billing: Sophie — I’ll prepare a one-off credit equal to 2x the reported missing tokens and note it as a customer goodwill credit. Also adding a bug reference for billing reconciliation.

sophie-support: Sent the offer to customer; they accepted temporary credit. They appreciated the quick turnaround.

elaine-engineer: Quick mitigation idea: change streaming accounting so that the final frame is applied before the refill job writes new bucket value, or add a small lease window that prevents refill until outstanding streams have a chance to finalize. Both have trade-offs; will prototype in staging and attach perf/complexity notes.

michael-support: Thanks all. Label follow-ups: #billing-action (jordan), #repro-staging (elaine), #customer-comms (sophie). We should also update support KB about the streaming-edge refill race so CS can surface it.

sophie-support: Noted — I’ll draft KB: short explainer + troubleshooting checklist (ask for stream_id, timestamps, screenshot).

ops-bot: Linked INC-2023-7145 to BUG-8452 (streaming finalization vs refill race).

michael-support: Closing thread for now — reopen if customer sees it again after the credit and staging fixes. :thumbsup:
